n: Payment Facilitator, High-Risk Merchant and Transaction Laundering
ds: Unauthorised or concealed merchants route card or bank payments through another merchant's account (transaction laundering) or use payment facilitators with weak sub-merchant oversight. This disguises illegal or high-risk goods and moves funds from fraud, gambling or illicit trade into the legitimate system.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Prepaid Cards, Mobile Payments and Internet-Based Payment Services (2013)
Card scheme rules on merchant and payment facilitator monitoring (general reference)
FATF, Risks of Gaming and Gambling (Red Flag Risk Indicators) (2026-09-09)

rat: Transaction laundering through sub-merchants of facilitators and acquirers.

ind.n: Transaction descriptors or products inconsistent with registered business
ind.cx: Card data show goods or services unrelated to the merchant's declared activity or website.
ind.ds: Card data show goods or services unrelated to the merchant's declared activity or website.

ind.n: Unusual ticket sizes or round amounts
ind.cx: Average ticket differs sharply from the merchant category or is repetitive and rounded.
ind.ds: Transactions are repeatedly in round or unusually uniform amounts that do not fit the stated purpose.

ind.cx: Chargebacks or refunds exceed scheme thresholds or peer averages.
ind.ds: Unusual refund or chargeback volumes or cycles relative to sales.

ind.n: Sub-merchants sharing owners, devices or bank accounts
ind.cx: Many sub-merchants link to the same individuals or accounts.
ind.ds: Several apparently separate businesses or sub-accounts share owners, signatories, addresses, devices or bank accounts.

ind.n: Website content differs from the underwriting file
ind.cx: Live site sells restricted products, redirects or has cloned or hidden pages.
ind.ds: Live site sells restricted products, redirects or has cloned or hidden pages.

ind.n: Rapid cash-out of settlements to third-party accounts
ind.cx: Settlement funds are sent immediately to unrelated accounts, often offshore.
ind.ds: Settlement funds are sent immediately to unrelated accounts, often offshore.

ind.cx: Sales volume arises from countries unrelated to the merchant's market.
ind.ds: Payments, counterparties or sales originate in or go to countries with no link to the customer, declared business, services or goods.
ind.cn: Payments or activity in jurisdictions unrelated to the customer's business or goods

ind.cx: Many small authorisations from varied cards, consistent with card testing then fraud.
ind.ds: Many small authorisations from varied cards, consistent with card testing then fraud.

ind.n: Payment facilitator onboarding lacks beneficial-owner data
ind.cx: Sub-merchants onboarded without full ownership or identity checks.
ind.ds: Sub-merchants onboarded without full ownership or identity checks.

ind.n: Use of multiple shell merchant accounts to spread volume
ind.cx: Volumes distributed across many accounts to stay below monitoring thresholds.
ind.ds: Volumes distributed across many accounts to stay below monitoring thresholds.

ind.n: Gambling payments disguised as ordinary retail purchases through sham merchants
ind.cx: Transaction laundering for gambling: sham merchants make gambling deposits look like retail sales.
ind.fp: Genuine retailers with mis-coded merchant category codes.
ind.ds: Card or account payments to what appears to be a domestic retailer are in fact deposits to an illicit gambling operator using a borrowed or fake merchant identity.

ctl.ds: Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

Verifies merchant identity, business model, website content and expected volumes before activation and re-verifies on change, with remediation of weak merchants. It stops fronts and disguised businesses entering payment channels.

Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

ctl.n: Counterparty VASP and platform due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses the licensing, AML controls, jurisdiction and reputation of counterparty exchanges, over-the-counter desks and other virtual asset service providers before enabling flows, and reviews them periodically. It limits exposure through weak or complicit counterparties.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

ctl.n: Risk appetite and product policy statements
ctl.ds: Documents the institution's appetite and permitted or prohibited products, assets and activities for a given risk area, with limits and review cadence. It gives staff and systems a clear boundary for acceptance.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.
